name: Sheba
title: The Rebel Against King David
summary: Sheba, son of Bichri, was a Benjaminite who led a rebellion against King David after Absalom's failed uprising. He sought to split Israel from Judah by inciting the northern tribes, but the revolt was crushed when the people of Abel Beth Maacah beheaded him and threw his head over the wall to Joab.

keyEvents.title: Sheba's Rebellion Against David
keyEvents.description: After Absalom's fall, Sheba blew the trumpet and declared that Israel had no share in David, urging the tribes to leave the king.

keyEvents.title: Israel Follows Sheba
keyEvents.description: All the men of Israel left David and followed Sheba son of Bichri, while the men of Judah remained loyal to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: David Sends Forces After Sheba
keyEvents.description: David ordered Amasa to gather the men of Judah within three days to pursue Sheba, fearing that Sheba might do more harm than Absalom.

keyEvents.title: Joab Kills Amasa
keyEvents.description: When Amasa was delayed, Joab took command and killed Amasa at the stone of Gibeon under the pretense of greeting him, before continuing the pursuit of Sheba.

keyEvents.title: The Siege of Abel-Beth-Maacah
keyEvents.description: Joab besieged the city of Abel-Beth-Maacah where Sheba had taken refuge and began to tear down the city wall.

keyEvents.title: A Wise Woman Ends the Rebellion
keyEvents.description: A wise woman in the city negotiated with Joab and persuaded the citizens to behead Sheba and throw his head over the wall, ending the rebellion.
